home_title: Texpile - a local, offline LaTeX and Typst editor
home_meta_description: Texpile is a free, open source editor for LaTeX, Typst, and Markdown. Edit visually or in source, compile with your own toolchain, all on your own machine.
home_social_description: Write LaTeX and Typst visually or in source, with live preview, byte-perfect saves, built-in git, and local compilation. Free and open source.
home_jsonld_feature_1: Visual and source editing for LaTeX, Typst, and Markdown
hero_heading: The LaTeX and Typst editor your writing deserves.
hero_body: See your document as you write it. Nothing leaves your machine.
live_preview_body: The page updates as you type, compiled by your own LaTeX. No manual compile. Math, TikZ, and pgfplots figures render live.
live_preview_video_aria: Live preview compiling as you type
editing_sub: One file, two ways to write it.
visual_editing_body: The editor parses your source and renders it as formatted text, math, tables, and figures. Anything it does not model stays as plain source, untouched.
formats_body: Your work stays in plain .tex, .typ, and .md files. What each format gets from the editor is not the same, so here is exactly what you can expect.
formats_latex_body: Visual and source editing, intellisense built from a static parse of your whole project, a live preview that retypesets as you type, and SyncTeX in both directions.
formats_latex_needs: Bring your own TeX distribution to compile.
formats_typst_body: Visual and source editing, with completion, hover, diagnostics, and rename from tinymist. The preview updates as you type without saving, and clicking the page jumps to the source line.
formats_md_body: Visual and source editing over plain .md files, with comments, shared sessions, spell check, math preview, and path completion for links and images.
formats_md_needs: Nothing to install. Texpile does not compile Markdown.
collab_body: Share a folder and edit it together in real time, in the visual editor or in source. Others join with a code, no sign up. End to end encrypted.
comments_body: Select anything and leave a comment. Works in the visual editor and in source, on LaTeX, Typst, and Markdown. Reply, resolve, and filter down to the file you are in.
comments_shot_alt: Writing a comment on a selected sentence, with the comment panel open below the editor
editing_point_1: Type @ to reference any equation, figure, table, or citation.
editing_point_2: Equations render inline and keep their numbering.
editing_point_3: Tables support multirow and multicolumn, edited visually.
editing_point_5: Drag or paste images in, then resize with handles.
editing_point_6: A math toolbar for equations, environments, and labels.
editing_point_4: Spell check skips your commands and math.
source_editing_body: A full source editor over the same file, with your whole project parsed for intellisense. Switch to visual and back, keeping scroll, cursor, and undo history.
typst_visual_1: Type @ to reference a figure, table, or citation.
typst_visual_2: Equations edit as math, not as markup.
typst_visual_3: Tables edit in place, with draggable column widths.
typst_visual_4: Drag or paste images in, then resize with handles.
typst_source_1: Completion and hover, provided by tinymist.
typst_source_2: Diagnostics appear as you type, with no compile step.
typst_source_3: F2 renames a symbol across the whole project.
typst_source_4: Click the preview to jump to the source line.
md_visual_1: Headings, lists, and quotes as formatted text.
md_visual_3: Tables edit in place, with draggable column widths.
md_visual_4: Drag or paste images in, then resize with handles.
md_source_1: Path completion inside links and image targets.
md_source_2: Shortcuts for headings, lists, and emphasis.
md_source_3: Equations preview live in the source editor.
md_source_4: Spell check that skips code and math.
intellisense_body: Texpile statically parses your whole project to produce intellisense.
intellisense_shot_alt: Source editor completing \cite with bibliography keys and titles
intellisense_point_3: References update when you rename or move a file.
intellisense_point_4: Your own \newcommand macros are picked up.
diagnostics_body: Texpile reads the compile log and the bibliography log into a Problems panel. Click a problem to jump to its line.
diagnostics_shot_alt: Problems panel showing a compile error with a plain-language explanation, followed by warnings
features_heading: More features that didn't get their own section
feature_palette_body: Ctrl+K opens a file, compiles, or runs any editor action.
feature_keymaps_body: Modal keybindings for the source editor, chosen in Preferences.
feature_multicursor_body: Add cursors down a column, or select the next occurrence.
feature_spellcheck_body: Checks your prose, skips commands, math, and comments.
feature_mcp_body: Connect Claude and other AI assistants to the editor.
feature_tabs_body: Reopen a folder and your tabs and cursor come back.
feature_synctex_body: Click in the PDF to jump to the source line, and back.
feature_terminal_body: A real shell for latexmk or any compile command.
feature_history_body: Stage, commit, and diff side-by-side against the last commit.
feature_sync_body: Switching keeps scroll, cursor, and undo history.
feature_multifile_body: Fragments parse with the main file's macros.
feature_math_body: Equations preview live in the source editor.
ps_body: Texpile is pronounced with the tex from text (tex-pile). The name is a blend of compiling LaTeX and transpiling it. We write it Texpile, not TeXpile.
dl_meta_description: Download Texpile, the free offline editor for LaTeX and Typst, for Windows, macOS, and Linux. No account required.
dl_subheading: Free and fully offline, for LaTeX, Typst, and Markdown. No account, no cloud, runs on your own machine.
dl_modal_star_prompt: While you wait, consider starring the project on GitHub to support it.
ty_visual_shot_alt: A Typst document in the visual editor: headings with their labels, formatted text, and lists

lx_title: Privacy-focused LaTeX editor with visual editing - Texpile
lx_meta_description: A free, open source desktop LaTeX editor for Windows, macOS, and Linux: visual and source editing, live preview, visual diff, comments, and collaboration.
lx_heading: A privacy-focused LaTeX editor for your most ambitious writing.
lx_lead: Texpile is an open source desktop LaTeX editor. It compiles the power of TeXstudio and LyX into a modern interface.
ty_title: Privacy-focused Typst editor with visual editing - Texpile
ty_meta_description: A free, open source desktop Typst editor for Windows, macOS, and Linux: visual and source editing, a live preview through tinymist, comments, and collaboration.
ty_heading: A privacy-focused Typst editor for your most ambitious writing.
ty_lead: Texpile is an open source desktop Typst editor. It brings the live preview of the Typst web app to your own computer, and adds a visual editor on top.
ty_preview_body: The document renders as you type in a pane beside the editor, through tinymist, with no save and no rebuild. An arrow shows the current line in the preview, and a click in the preview jumps back to the source line.
ty_preview_shot_alt: The Typst preview beside the source editor, rendering the document as it is typed
ty_needs_body: One program, tinymist. It compiles the document and provides the completion, hover help, and errors. Editing works without it.
fmt_history_shot_alt: The visual editor showing a heading and a sentence changed since the last version
lx_ways_sub: Unlike LyX, Texpile stores nothing but .tex. Write in source or write visually, in the same file, and it is saved back with only your edits changed.
lx_preview_body: The page updates as you type. Texpile injects its own scripts into your LuaTeX engine, so a text edit re-typesets its paragraph in a few milliseconds instead of recompiling the document.
lx_also_sub: The features every LaTeX editor has. They did not earn a section of their own.
lx_needs_line: Compiles with your own TeX distribution: TeX Live, MacTeX, or MiKTeX. Editing works without one.
ed_reviews_sub: Write like an author, not a developer.
ed_diff_body: A changed file opens as a diff against the last version, in whichever editor you are in. The visual editor marks the changes in the formatted text, word by word. The source editor shows them side by side, line by line.
ed_speed_body: From launch to the main window, warm start, median of five runs, measured on one Windows 11 laptop in September 2026.
ed_speed_vscode_note: If VS Code is also your editor for everything else and carries many extensions, it starts more slowly than this.
ed_themes_body: Light or dark mode, and a color theme for the whole window, picked in Preferences.
ed_themes_shot_alt: Preferences › Appearance: the Mode tiles and the theme tiles
ed_ways_heading: Two ways to write a document
